title: Frequency‑Aware Flow Matching for Continuous and Consistent Robotic Action Generation
claim: Discretized chunked representations cause gradient conflict and jittery outputs; a frequency-domain representation with velocity supervision fixes both.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right: setup, two failure modes, method with outcome
description: A three-column figure read left to right. The left column shows a physical action trajectory over a filmstrip of a robot arm. It is sampled and chunked into a discrete chunked action representation, drawn as a red dotted curve over chunk indices. The middle column has two red-tinted problem boxes. Box 1, 'Mixed frequencies → Identifiability Failure', shows 5, 10 and 20 Hz trajectories with fixed-horizon chunks feeding a red 'Gradient Conflict' node. Beside it is a gradient cosine similarity axis where 'Ours' scores +0.87 and 'Chunk style' scores -0.65. Box 2, 'Lack of dynamics constraints → High-frequency jitter', contrasts a smooth demonstration with a jagged predicted path. The right column is a green method panel. It shows low, mid and high frequency inputs going through a DCT formula, flow matching with a velocity field, a velocity supervision plot, and the combined loss L_FAFM. These feed a bar chart of frequency-space coefficients. A blue box at the bottom shows a smoother trajectory leading to stable manipulation.
caption: Introduction overview. Action chunk discretization causes Identifiability Failure and high-frequency jitter, which FAFM resolves via frequency-domain flow matching and velocity supervision.
abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a standard paradigm for robotic manipulation owing to its strong expressive power for modelling complex, multimodal action distributions, alongside similar approaches like diffusion policy. However, existing methods rely on discretized action chunks, making them brittle to demonstrations collected at heterogeneous control frequencies and prone to temporally inconsistent actions that degrade control stability. In this paper, we propose Frequency-Aware Flow Matching (FAFM), which outputs continuous, temporally consistent actions. To handle heterogeneous frequency input, we transform discrete action sequences into the frequency domain with the discrete cosine transform (DCT), perform flow matching over the resulting coefficients, and reconstruct continuous actions via cosine basis expansion. To generate temporally consistent actions, we regularize the first-order temporal derivative to promote smooth actions. This corresponds to a Sobolev-type constraint that suppresses high-frequency errors and discourages abrupt action changes. Our FAFM is simple, introduces no additional network parameters and applies to standalone flow-matching policies and vision-language action models. Across synthetic toy benchmark, obstacle avoidance, LapGym, and LIBERO, FAFM improves success rates, multimodal expressivity, motion smoothness, convergence speed, robustness to mechanical bias and mixed-frequency input. These gains are consistent when deployed on a real-world Franka robot. Code available at https://github.com/gakakulicc/FAFM.
